                 lag(okun.ts[,2], -1),

Taxa de desemprego (du/dt) explicada pelo crescimento econômico (g[t], g[t-1], g[t-2])

\[ \dfrac{\rm{d}u}{\rm{d}t} \approx \dfrac{u_t-u_{t-1}}{t-(t-1)} = \dfrac{u_t-u_{t-1}}{1} = u_t-u_{t-1} = d(u) \]

okunL2.dyn <- dynlm(d(u)~L(g, 0:2), data=okun.ts)
okunL2.dyn %>% summary
## 
## Time series regression with "ts" data:
## Start = 1985(4), End = 2009(3)
##

## L(g, 0:2)2  -0.07001    0.03310  -2.115   0.0371 *

1.3 Serial correlation

layout(1:3 %>% matrix(nrow = 1))
plot(okun.ts[,"g"], ylab="growth")
plot(okun.ts[,"u"], ylab="unemployment")
plot(okun.ts[,"u"] %>% diff, ylab="diff(unemployment)")

ggL3 <- data.frame(cbind(okun.ts[,"g"], lag(okun.ts[,"g"],-1), lag(okun.ts[,"g"],-2), lag(okun.ts[,"g"],-3)))
cor(ggL3, use = "pairwise")
##                         okun.ts....g.. lag.okun.ts....g.....1.
## okun.ts....g..               1.0000000               0.4957684
## lag.okun.ts....g.....1.      0.4957684               1.0000000
## lag.okun.ts....g.....2.      0.4269941               0.4957684
## lag.okun.ts....g.....3.      0.1768312               0.4269941
##                         lag.okun.ts....g.....2. lag.okun.ts....g.....3.
## okun.ts....g..                        0.4269941               0.1768312
## lag.okun.ts....g.....1.               0.4957684               0.4269941
## lag.okun.ts....g.....2.               1.0000000               0.4957684
## lag.okun.ts....g.....3.               0.4957684               1.0000000

\[ z = \dfrac{r_k}{\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{T}}}\\ r_k = z\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{T}}\\ z \in \{-1.96, 1.96\}\\ T = 98 \\ r_k =\{-1.96, 1.96\}\times\sqrt{1/98}\approx \{-0.198, 0.198\} \]

acf(okun.ts[,"g"]) -> v

inf~d(u)

data("phillips_aus", package="PoEdata")
phill.ts <- ts(phillips_aus, 
               start=c(1987,1), 
               end=c(2009,3),
               frequency=4)
plot.ts(phill.ts)

plot.ts(diff(phill.ts[,"u"]))

dynlm(inf~d(u), data = phill.ts) -> phill.dyn
ehat <- phill.dyn$residuals
plot(ehat)
abline(h=0, lty=2)

acf(ehat)

library(lmtest)
bgtest(phill.dyn, 1)
## 
##  Breusch-Godfrey test for serial correlation of order up to 1
## 
## data:  phill.dyn
## LM test = 27.592, df = 1, p-value = 1.498e-07
bgtest(phill.dyn, 4)
## 
##  Breusch-Godfrey test for serial correlation of order up to 4
## 
## data:  phill.dyn
## LM test = 36.672, df = 4, p-value = 2.105e-07
dwtest(phill.dyn)
## 
##  Durbin-Watson test
## 
## data:  phill.dyn
## DW = 0.88729, p-value = 2.198e-09
## alternative hypothesis: true autocorrelation is greater than 0

1.4 Estimation with Serially Correlated Errors

library(sandwich)
s1 <- coeftest(phill.dyn, vcov.=vcovHAC(phill.dyn))
stargazer::stargazer(phill.dyn, s1, type = "text")

1.5 9.6 A More General Model

acf(phill.ts[, "inf"])

pacf(phill.ts[, "inf"])

\[ \text{inf}_t = b_0 + b_1 \text{inf}_{t-1} + b_2 \text{du}_t + e_t \]

dynlm(inf~L(inf, 1:2)+d(u), data = phill.ts) -> phill.gen
plot(phill.gen$residuals); abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

bgtest(phill.gen, 1)
## 
##  Breusch-Godfrey test for serial correlation of order up to 1
## 
## data:  phill.gen
## LM test = 1.4112, df = 1, p-value = 0.2349
dwtest(phill.gen)
## 
##  Durbin-Watson test
## 
## data:  phill.gen
## DW = 2.0699, p-value = 0.5861
## alternative hypothesis: true autocorrelation is greater than 0
shapiro.test(phill.gen$residuals)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  phill.gen$residuals
## W = 0.96445, p-value = 0.0154
mhist(phill.gen$residuals)

reset(phill.gen)
## 
##  RESET test
## 
## data:  phill.gen
## RESET = 2.1335, df1 = 2, df2 = 83, p-value = 0.1249
bptest(phill.gen)
## 
##  studentized Breusch-Pagan test
## 
## data:  phill.gen
## BP = 9.2786, df = 3, p-value = 0.02581
# vou usar a correção de heteroscedasticidade porque 
# o teste de Breusch-Pagan rejeitou H0
coeftest(phill.gen, vcov. = vcovHAC(phill.gen))
## 
## t test of coefficients:
## 
##              Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)   
## (Intercept)   0.25500    0.08477  3.0082 0.003457 **
## L(inf, 1:2)1  0.37445    0.12634  2.9638 0.003942 **
## L(inf, 1:2)2  0.27133    0.12526  2.1661 0.033104 * 
## d(u)         -0.57442    0.20816 -2.7595 0.007089 **
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

1.6 9.7 Autoregressive Models

Explico uma variável em função dela mesma em períodos passados.

\[ y_t = b_0 + \sum b_i y_{t-i} + e_t \]

okun.ts %>% head
##        g   u
## [1,] 1.4 7.3
## [2,] 2.0 7.2
## [3,] 1.4 7.0
## [4,] 1.5 7.0
## [5,] 0.9 7.2
## [6,] 1.5 7.0
formula = g~L(g, 1:2)
dynlm(formula, data = okun.ts) -> okun.ar2
summary(okun.ar2)
## 
## Time series regression with "ts" data:
## Start = 1985(4), End = 2009(3)
##

## dynlm(formula = formula, data = okun.ts)

## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)   0.4657     0.1433   3.251 0.001602 ** 
## L(g, 1:2)1    0.3770     0.1000   3.769 0.000287 ***
## L(g, 1:2)2    0.2462     0.1029   2.394 0.018686 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.5527 on 93 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.2907, Adjusted R-squared:  0.2754 
## F-statistic: 19.06 on 2 and 93 DF,  p-value: 1.159e-07
shapiro.test(okun.ar2$residuals)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
##

2 Gerando dados correlacionados

# Gerando séries temporais
set.seed(12)
N = 200
NN = N*1.2
arcompy = c(0.5, 0.4, 0.0)
arcompx = c(0.4, -0.3, 0.0)
y = rnorm(NN)
x = rnorm(NN)
erro = 0.2*rnorm(NN)
# Série autoregressiva
y = arima.sim(list(ar = arcompy), n = NN)
# adiciona o efeito de x
for(i in (length(arcompy)+1):NN) {
  y[i] = y[i]+arcompx[1]*x[i]+arcompx[2]*x[i-1]+arcompx[3]*x[i-2]
}
# adiciona o termo de erro
for(i in (length(arcompy)+1):NN) {
  y[i] = y[i]+erro[i]
}
# coloca em um data frame
dd = data.frame(y = y[(NN-N+1):NN], x = x[(NN-N+1):NN])
# inspecionando para ver como ficou
plot.ts(dd)

# PACF indica 2 lags para a autoregressão
pacf(dd[,'y'])

# Cross-Correlation indica efeito de x contemporâneo e 1 atraso
ccf(dd[,'y'], dd[,'x'])

# transforma os dados em série temporal
dd = ts(dd)
# varre os possíveis modelos guardando o BIC
nmod = 0
mlist = list()
aics = NULL
frms = NULL
for(ary in 0:4) {
  for(arx in 0:4) {
    if(ary == 0) {
      frm = paste0("y~L(x, 0:", arx, ")") %>% as.formula
      dynlm(frm, dd) -> m
    } else {
      frm = paste0("y~L(y, 1:", ary, ")+L(x, 0:", arx, ")") %>% as.formula
      dynlm(frm, dd) -> m
    }
    nmod = nmod + 1
    aics = c(aics, BIC(m))
    mlist[[nmod]] = m
    frms = c(frms, frm)
  }
}
# vê qual modelo possui o menor BIC
nmod = which.min(aics)
# Pega esse modelo
mlist[[nmod]] -> m
# mostra a equação
frms[nmod]
## [[1]]
## y ~ L(y, 1:2) + L(x, 0:1)
## <environment: 0x1114e69d0>
# forma funcional
reset(m)
## 
##  RESET test
## 
## data:  m
## RESET = 0.38475, df1 = 2, df2 = 191, p-value = 0.6811
# autoregressão
bgtest(m)

## 
## data:  m
## LM test = 0.33679, df = 1, p-value = 0.5617
# Heteroscedasticidade
bptest(m)
## 
##  studentized Breusch-Pagan test
## 
## data:  m
## BP = 2.7449, df = 4, p-value = 0.6014
# Normalidade dos resíduos
shapiro.test(m$residuals)

## 
## data:  m$residuals
## W = 0.99286, p-value = 0.4503
mhist(m$residuals)

plot.ts(m$residuals)

boxplot(m$residuals)

# tudo ok, vamos aos coeficientes
